4354.title: Reward
4354.heading: Reward
4354.content:
A reward is positive feedback that pulls a player toward an action, goal, or further engagement. It can mark a milestone, confirm that the player is on a productive path, or open new parts of the game's [[Possibility Space]].

The feeling of reward depends on the effort and context leading to it, not only on celebratory images or sound. Reward signals are most meaningful at significant moments rather than after every routine action.

4357.title: Return on Investment
4357.heading: Return on Investment
4357.content:
Return on investment compares the financial benefit produced by an initiative with the capital committed to it. For a big-data project, value comes from improved decisions, lower cost, new revenue, or faster processes rather than the quantity of data collected.

Timing, risk, dependencies, and the opportunity to fund a different project make simple benefit-minus-cost totals incomplete.

A basic calculation expresses ROI as the gain from an investment minus its cost, divided by that cost. When gains and costs occur at different times, an adjusted comparison should use [[Net Present Value]] rather than treating every cash flow as if it occurred immediately.

4360.title: Reversible Computing
4360.heading: Reversible Computing
4360.content:
Reversible computing uses operations whose inputs can be reconstructed uniquely from their outputs. By avoiding the routine erasure of information, it offers a theoretical route to reducing the energy dissipated by conventional computation.

Reversibility changes familiar programming assumptions because intermediate information cannot simply disappear. Algorithms and hardware must preserve enough state to undo each transformation.

4363.sourceSearchName: reversing an inequality reversing an inequality
4363.title: Reversing an Inequality
4363.heading: Reversing an Inequality
4363.content:
Reversing an inequality changes (<) to (>) or (\leq) to (\geq), and conversely. It is required when both sides are multiplied or divided by a negative number.

For (-2x\leq-10), division by (-2) gives (x\geq5). The reversal occurs because multiplication by a negative reflects ordered points across zero on the [[Number Line]]. Forgetting it produces the opposite solution set. Adding or subtracting a negative number does not itself trigger reversal; the rule concerns multiplication or division by a negative value.

4366.title: Reverse Proxy
4366.heading: Reverse Proxy
4366.content:
A reverse proxy accepts client traffic on behalf of an application server and forwards requests to that server. It provides the public HTTP and HTTPS boundary while the application can listen on an internal address.

In the Linux deployment, [[Nginx]] proxies requests to [[Kestrel]]. Because the connection seen by Kestrel originates at the proxy, [[Forwarded Headers Middleware]] restores information about the original client request.

A confirmed earlier match can strongly clarify [[Image Provenance]], especially when dates and context contradict the current claim. Searching distinctive fragments separately can help when a composite contains material drawn from multiple sources.

4372.content:
Reverse image search is limited by what a provider has indexed and by how strongly an uploaded query resembles stored images. A failed search does not show that a photograph is original; the source may be private, newly published, heavily edited, or absent from the index.

Uploading a sensitive image also discloses evidence to the search provider and may create privacy or investigative risks. The method is therefore most informative when it finds a credible match, while a nonmatch must remain an inconclusive result.

4375.heading: Retopology in Blender
4375.content:
Retopology rebuilds a clean mesh over a dense or irregular sculpt. The sculpt supplies the form, while a new mesh uses more deliberate edge flow and a lower, more even component count.

Blender's native workflow combines ordinary modeling tools with surface snapping. Afterward, important detail from the high-resolution sculpt can be reintroduced through modeling or baked textures.

For game assets, retopology separates the mesh used to author fine form from the lower-complexity mesh used at runtime. The appropriate reduction is relative to target hardware, viewing distance, deformation needs, and the asset's importance within the environment.

4384.title: Resultant Force
4384.heading: Resultant Force
4384.content: The resultant force is the vector sum of all external forces acting on an object. A zero resultant produces translational equilibrium or constant velocity; a nonzero resultant produces acceleration according to [[Newton's Second Law]]. Forces may be added graphically or resolved into perpendicular components before their component sums are recombined.

4387.heading: Restricted Boltzmann Machine
4387.content:
A restricted Boltzmann machine is an undirected probabilistic model with visible and hidden units and no connections within either layer. The restricted structure makes conditional sampling and learning more tractable than in a fully connected Boltzmann machine.

Hidden-unit activations form learned features of the visible input. Training adjusts weights so that the model assigns greater probability to observed patterns, commonly using approximations to otherwise expensive likelihood gradients.

4396.title: Responsible Innovation
4396.heading: Responsible Innovation
4396.content:
Responsible innovation is an approach to research and development that anticipates consequences, reflects on values, includes stakeholders, and responds to new evidence. It shifts ethical attention from repairing harm after deployment to shaping the direction and conditions of innovation itself.

The approach requires both process and substance. Inclusive discussion helps reveal who bears risk, while design methods translate values into technical and organizational choices. Responsibility also requires an option not to proceed. If innovation is treated as inevitable, participation can become a way to secure acceptance rather than a real opportunity to alter or stop the project.

4399.title: Responsibility Gap
4399.heading: Responsibility Gap
4399.content:
A responsibility gap appears when an AI system causes a morally significant outcome but no actor seems to satisfy the usual conditions for full responsibility. The machine may operate with some autonomy while lacking moral understanding, and the people involved may neither control nor foresee its particular action.

The gap is a governance problem, not proof that nobody should answer. It can be reduced by assigning duties before deployment, maintaining oversight, documenting the [[Data Science Pipeline]], and ensuring that organizations can investigate and remedy harm. Treating the system itself as responsible may instead widen the gap by shielding human decision makers.

4402.title: Resource
4402.heading: Resource
4402.content:
A resource is something countable that can be generated, stored, transferred, exchanged, converted, or removed within a [[System]]. It may be physical, such as wood, or abstract, such as health, time, movement, or experience.

Resources flow among functional roles such as [[System Source]], [[Stock]], [[Converter]], and [[System Sink]]. A simple resource is interchangeable with others of its type, while a complex resource may be assembled from simpler resources and carry distinct attributes.

Within games, a resource can enable a verb: ammunition permits shooting, currency permits spending, and health determines how much harm can be endured before a setback. Because resources are countable, they support decisions about saving, spending, and accepting risk.

4405.heading: Resource Utilization Power Model
4405.content:
A resource utilization power model predicts energy consumption from observed use of processors, memory, storage, and network interfaces. Coefficients approximate how much each resource adds to a machine's baseline demand.

Such a model is useful for online control when direct component measurements are unavailable. Its accuracy depends on workload type, hardware state, and interactions that a simple linear estimate may omit.

4408.title: Resource Pooling
4408.heading: Resource Pooling
4408.content:
Resource pooling combines computing, storage, or networking capacity so that it can be assigned among consumers according to demand. Pooling raises utilization because idle capacity from one workload can serve another rather than remaining tied to one dedicated machine.

Virtualized resources are well suited to a pool because software can create, move, and release instances automatically. When several consumers share the resulting service, the pool also supports [[Multi-Tenancy]] and [[Rapid Elasticity]].

4414.title: Resource Flow
4414.heading: Resource Flow
4414.content:
Resource flow describes how quantified entities enter, move through, change ownership within, convert inside, and leave an internal economy. Mapping sources, drains, stores, traders, and converters exposes the structure behind changing totals.

A flow diagram can reveal mutual dependencies, feedback loops, exploits, and stalled production before they are buried in implementation. An entity that never changes or transfers is not functioning as a resource.

4417.title: Resonance
4417.heading: Resonance
4417.content: Resonance is the large steady response of a driven oscillator when the driving frequency is near its natural frequency. Energy is then transferred efficiently on successive cycles. Weak damping produces a tall, narrow resonance peak, while stronger damping reduces the maximum amplitude and spreads the response across a broader frequency range.

4419.sourceSearchName: resonance in air columns resonance in air columns

4420.sourceSearchName: resonance in air columns resonance in air columns
4420.title: Resonance in Air Columns
4420.heading: Resonance in Air Columns
4420.content: An air column resonates when its length supports a [[Standing Wave]] consistent with its ends. An open end is approximately a displacement antinode, while a closed end is a displacement node. A tube open at both ends supports integer harmonics; a tube closed at one end supports the odd harmonics in the ideal model.

4423.content:
A resilient distributed dataset is Spark's partitioned collection abstraction for parallel transformations and actions. It can cache working data in memory and records lineage so a lost partition can be recomputed from earlier transformations.

Immutability and lineage simplify recovery, while partitioning and persistence choices determine locality, communication, and memory pressure.

4426.title: Residue Field
4426.heading: Residue Field
4426.content:
For a [[Local Ring]] (R,m), the residue field is the [[Quotient Ring]] R/m. It is a [[Field]] because m is a [[Maximal Ideal]].

Reducing a module modulo m turns it into a vector space over the residue field. [[Nakayama's Lemma]] uses the dimension of this vector space to identify a minimal number of generators.

4429.title: Residual
4429.heading: Residual
4429.content:
A residual is the difference between an observed outcome and the value predicted by a fitted model. Residuals represent the portion of each observation not explained by the model's current terms.

Their distribution and relationship with fitted values or predictors support assumption checks. Systematic curvature, changing spread, or extreme residuals can reveal misspecification that a high-level fit statistic conceals.

4431.sourceSearchName: residual sum of squares residual sum of squares
4431.title: Residual Sum of Squares
4431.heading: Document

4432.sourceSearchName: residual sum of squares residual sum of squares
4432.title: Residual Sum of Squares
4432.heading: Residual Sum of Squares
4432.content:
The residual sum of squares is $\sum_i(y_i-\hat y_i)^2$, the total squared vertical discrepancy between observed and fitted values.

Squaring prevents positive and negative residuals from cancelling and penalizes larger discrepancies more strongly. [[Least Squares Approximation]] selects parameters that make this quantity as small as possible.

4435.title: Residual Skip Connection
4435.heading: Residual Skip Connection
4435.content:
A skip connection sends the output of one neural-network layer directly to a later layer instead of requiring all information to pass through every intervening layer. Kelleher describes ResNet as an extension of the [[Convolutional Neural Network]] architecture that uses such connections to train very deep networks.

The bypass changes the network's information path while retaining the ordinary layered transformations. It is a structural response to the difficulty of training deep models, alongside methods such as improved initialization and activation functions. The book's 152-layer ResNet example illustrates the scale made possible by this design, not a general rule that depth alone improves accuracy.

4438.sourceSearchName: researcher degrees of freedom researcher degrees of freedom
4438.title: Researcher Degrees of Freedom
4438.heading: Researcher Degrees of Freedom
4438.content:
Researcher degrees of freedom are the analytic choices available in variable definition, exclusions, transformations, model form, covariate selection, interactions, and reporting. When these choices are made after seeing results, they can steer an analysis toward a preferred conclusion.

Prespecification, a restricted candidate set, versioned code, and [[Model Metadata]] make this flexibility visible. Judgment remains necessary, but transparent constraints help distinguish model development from [[P-Hacking]].

4441.title: Resampling Periodicity
4441.heading: Resampling Periodicity
4441.content:
Resampling periodicity is the repeating pattern of prediction relationships created when an interpolation grid passes through an original pixel lattice. At some output positions the value depends strongly on a particular arrangement of neighbors, and that arrangement recurs at intervals determined by the scale or rotation.

A detector estimates local linear dependencies and searches their strength for periodic structure. A localized response can expose a transformed insert, whereas an image-wide response may simply record benign resizing during publication.

4444.title: Requirements Specification
4444.heading: Requirements Specification
4444.content: A requirements specification records requested capabilities, constraints, or expected behavior, but it is an incomplete substitute for direct domain learning. It can freeze assumptions, emphasize features over the underlying [[Problem Space]], and omit tacit knowledge that experts consider obvious. Treating it as an input to [[Knowledge Crunching]] rather than as unquestionable truth allows conversations, prototypes, and models to reveal contradictions and clarify what outcome the software must support.

4447.title: Requirements Analysis
4447.heading: Requirements Analysis
4447.content:
Requirements analysis investigates intended users, their activities, and their environment before a new design is built. Here, work includes employment, learning, play, or any activity the system is meant to support.

Contextual inquiry gathers evidence through observation, interviews, recordings, and existing work artifacts. Contextual analysis organizes and interprets that evidence into models of users, tasks, relationships, artifacts, and physical settings. Requirements are then extracted from the problems and opportunities found.

This work grounds [[User-Centered Design]] in actual context and supplies inputs to [[Task Analysis]], design, and [[Prototype|prototyping]].

4450.content:
A reputation system attack manipulates aggregated trust evidence rather than improving the underlying behavior. Newcomer attacks repeatedly discard bad identities, self-boosting raises an attacker's score, bad-mouthing lowers a target, and on-off behavior alternates honesty with abuse.

Robust models consider rater reliability, time, uncertainty, collusion, and the cost of creating a fresh identity.

Reproducibility depends on more than saved code. It also requires stable source data, [[External Data Dictionary|external metadata]], explicit software dependencies, recorded modeling decisions, and output names that consistently point later stages to the current analytic dataset.

4462.title: Representative Player
4462.heading: Representative Player
4462.content:
A representative player is a hypothetical person who typifies the intended target audience. The designer uses this figure to evaluate whether a proposed feature, challenge, interface, or theme serves the experience being built.

The representative is a decision aid rather than a stereotype or claim about every customer. It should be grounded in audience research and revised when observation contradicts the assumptions behind it.

4465.heading: Replaced and Nonreplaced Elements
4465.content:
A replaced element is rendered using content outside the document itself, such as an image supplied through a URL or a form control drawn by the user agent. CSS generally treats that external object as a unit with intrinsic dimensions instead of laying out its internal contents.

A nonreplaced element has content represented within the document tree, so CSS constructs and formats boxes for that content directly. The distinction affects sizing, baselines, and inline formatting in the [[CSS Box Model]].

Tags: [[Dapper Data Access]] [[Aggregate Consistency and Persistence]]

4468.title: Repository Pattern
4468.heading: Repository Pattern
4468.content:
The repository pattern places persistence operations behind an application-facing interface. Controllers request domain data through repository methods instead of embedding connections and SQL inside HTTP actions.

With Dapper, the repository owns query text, parameters, result mapping, and connection behavior. This boundary makes callers less dependent on the chosen access mechanism and gives tests a replaceable data collaborator.

The inventory example first puts books in an in-memory repository shared by add, update, and get commands, then plans to replace that store with persistent data. The command logic can stay focused on its operation because the repository interface, not the initial storage choice, is its dependency.

In Domain-Driven Design, a repository represents a collection of [[Aggregate]] roots and abstracts their persistence from the domain and application layers. Its interface can load or add an aggregate while a separate [[Unit of Work]] owns the commit. A repository should not become a generic query layer for arbitrary screens: aggregate behavior belongs on the command side, while [[Read Model]] queries can use storage directly when that better matches their purpose.

4470.sourceSearchName: repetition as punishment repetition as punishment
4470.title: Repetition as Punishment
4470.heading: Document

4471.sourceSearchName: repetition as punishment repetition as punishment
4471.title: Repetition as Punishment
4471.heading: Repetition as Punishment
4471.content:
Repetition as punishment requires a player to replay part of a game after failure. Returning to a [[Checkpoint]] can make the earlier sequence the price of another attempt without permanently removing the opportunity to continue.

Repetition can serve as practice when it returns the player to an unmastered challenge or an open situation that can unfold differently. Once the repeated actions are already mastered and fixed, it increasingly becomes rote time cost rather than useful learning.

4477.title: Repeating Decimal
4477.heading: Repeating Decimal
4477.content:
A repeating decimal has a finite block of digits that continues indefinitely, such as

$$0.090909\ldots=0.\overline{09}.$$

Every repeating decimal is a [[Rational Number]]. To convert one to a fraction, let a variable equal the decimal, multiply by powers of ten until two forms share the same infinite tail, and subtract. For (x=0.\overline{09}), (100x-x=9), so (99x=9) and (x=1/11). A terminating decimal is also rational because trailing zeros make it a repeating form.

4498.title: Remainder Theorem
4498.heading: Remainder Theorem
4498.content: When a [[Polynomial]] $f(x)$ is divided by $x-c$, the remainder is $f(c)$. The statement follows from polynomial division: $f(x)=(x-c)q(x)+r$, where the remainder $r$ is constant; substituting $x=c$ gives $f(c)=r$. The theorem turns substitution into a shortcut for testing a proposed divisor.

4501.title: Remote Collaboration
4501.heading: Remote Collaboration
4501.content:
Remote collaboration connects participants who occupy different physical locations but work on a shared task or representation. AR can combine live video, reconstructed geometry, virtual objects, annotations, pointing, and speech to make one participant's environment accessible to another.

The collaborators may have different devices, views, and roles. The system must communicate what each person can see or control and keep shared spatial references synchronized across the network.

4504.heading: Relevant Component Analysis
4504.content:
Relevant component analysis learns a linear metric from groups of observations connected by must-link constraints. These connected components, called chunklets, provide examples of variability that should not separate similar cases.

The method estimates within-chunklet covariance and whitens the data relative to it. Directions of irrelevant variation are suppressed, while differences not explained inside the chunklets receive greater importance in the resulting Mahalanobis distance.

4507.title: Release Planning
4507.heading: Release Planning
4507.content:
Release planning establishes a shared goal and forecasts how ordered backlog work may fit across several Sprints. The result connects product vision, likely Sprint Goals, scope, and a target date without claiming certainty.

The forecast is revised after every Sprint using completed work and newly discovered information. Scope or time changes when actual [[Velocity]] differs from the assumptions.

Reliable message delivery uses an acknowledgment or handshake to give the sender evidence that a message or ordered block of messages reached the receiver. If acknowledgment does not arrive, the system can retain or resend the work according to its policy.

Reliability reduces silent loss but does not by itself guarantee one-time processing. Retries can produce duplicate delivery unless message identity and consumer behavior make repeated work safe.

4516.heading: Release Pipeline
4516.content:
A release pipeline takes versioned build artifacts and installs them into one or more deployment environments. In the book, the flow targets Azure staging resources before promoting a verified release to production.

Separating release from build means the same tested artifact can move between environments. Environment configuration and promotion conditions remain part of the release definition rather than the compiled package.

4519.title: Relaxation Factor
4519.heading: Relaxation Factor
4519.content:
A relaxation factor $\omega$ controls how strongly an iterative method accepts a newly computed correction. The update combines the previous value with the candidate value.

In [[Successive Over-Relaxation]], $\omega=1$ gives the [[Gauss-Seidel Method]], $0<\omega<1$ gives under-relaxation, and $1<\omega<2$ gives over-relaxation. The best value depends on the problem.

4531.content: Relative humidity compares the actual water-vapor content or pressure with the saturation value at the same temperature. Because saturation capacity changes with temperature, air can approach saturation through cooling even when no water vapor is added. The result links [[Dry-Bulb and Wet-Bulb Temperature]] to dew point, fog, cloud, and icing risk.

4534.title: Relative Estimation
4534.heading: Relative Estimation
4534.content:
Relative estimation compares the size and complexity of one backlog item with known examples instead of predicting an exact duration. Teams use analogy and triangulation to place items on a shared scale.

Comparison is often more reliable than absolute forecasting under uncertainty. The estimate supports planning, while actual throughput remains the evidence used to revise future forecasts.

4537.title: Relative Difficulty
4537.heading: Relative Difficulty
4537.content:
Relative difficulty compares a challenge's absolute difficulty with the power the game gives the player to meet it. Health, equipment, abilities, information, allies, and permitted actions can all change that power.

The same enemy can therefore be difficult for a weak character and easy for a developed one. Progression must coordinate challenge growth with the player's changing capabilities.

4540.title: Relative Error
4540.heading: Relative Error
4540.content:
Relative error divides [[Absolute Error]] by the magnitude of the exact value: $|x-x^*|/|x|$, when $x\neq0$.

It expresses error as a proportion of the quantity being approximated. Multiplying by 100 gives percentage error, while the number of correct significant digits can be related to a sufficiently small relative error.

Protecting one person's relationship also affects the other endpoint, so disclosure choices cannot always be modeled as independent individual settings.

4552.title: Relational Database
4552.heading: Relational Database
4552.content:
A relational database stores data in tables that are mathematical relations: sets of ordered tuples drawn from Cartesian products of data types. Rows are tuples or records, and named columns identify their components.

SQL queries select rows by predicates, project chosen columns, and combine tables through joins that begin from a product and retain matching records. A database management system also supports insertion, deletion, updating, and query optimization.

4555.content:
Relational moral status treats moral consideration as something formed through social interaction rather than derived only from hidden internal properties. A robot can enter patterns of care, address, dependence, and recognition that change how people understand what may be done to it.

The approach explains why status can differ across settings and cultures and why people may respond morally to a machine without evidence of [[Machine Sentience]]. It also creates a risk of projection: designers can manufacture cues that invite attachment. Ethical analysis must therefore examine both the lived relationship and the power of those who designed its terms.

4564.title: Rejection Sampling
4564.heading: Rejection Sampling
4564.content:
Rejection sampling proposes values from an easier distribution and accepts each according to a probability determined by the target-to-proposal ratio. Accepted values follow the target when the scaled proposal bounds it everywhere.

The method produces unweighted target samples, but its efficiency depends on how tightly the proposal covers the target. A loose bound causes most candidates to be rejected.

4567.title: Reinforcing Loop
4567.heading: Reinforcing Loop
4567.content:
A reinforcing loop amplifies the direction of change already occurring in a system. The reinforced quality may be desirable or harmful: growth, learning, disease spread, and accumulating advantage can share the same structure.

In games, reinforcing loops support gain and [[Progression System|progression]], but an unchecked loop can produce a rich-get-richer outcome and collapse the [[Play Space]]. [[Balancing Loop|Balancing loops]] can preserve meaningful competition by limiting runaway divergence.

4570.title: Reinforcement Learning
4570.heading: Reinforcement Learning
4570.content:
Reinforcement learning trains an agent by rewarding or penalizing the consequences of its actions. The agent learns a policy that chooses actions expected to accumulate useful future reward.

In a conversational system, actions can include asking a question, confirming a value, or completing a task. Learning must balance the [[Exploration-Exploitation Tradeoff]] while avoiding harmful experiments on real users.

Kelleher describes a policy that maps an agent's observation and internal state to its next action. The agent can learn while acting in an environment, so use and training are interleaved. A reward may arrive only after several actions, as when a game gives its outcome at the end; assigning that feedback to earlier decisions is therefore a central training challenge. This differs from [[Supervised Learning]], where each example already carries its desired target output.

In automated business analytics, reinforcement learning can also guide a multistage forecasting procedure. The source combines it with generalized optimal wavelet decomposition so reward signals help select transformations and forecasting choices evaluated on data.

Inside the Jacobson radical, permutations and positive powers preserve regularity under the source's Noetherian finite-generation hypotheses. The maximum possible length in an ideal defines [[Depth of a Module]].

This theorem makes regularity stable under moving to a smaller neighborhood of the spectrum. It supports the definition of a [[Regular Ring]] through all prime localizations.

4591.content:
A Noetherian ring is regular when every localization R_p at a [[Prime Ideal]] is a [[Regular Local Ring]]. Regularity is therefore defined pointwise across the spectrum.

For a regular local ring, the residue field has finite projective dimension equal to the Krull dimension. Polynomial rings over a field satisfy the corresponding finite-resolution bound through the Hilbert syzygy theorem.

Those generators form a [[Regular System of Parameters]]. The homological characterization says R is regular exactly when its residue field has finite [[Projective Dimension]].

4597.heading: Regular Expression
4597.content:
A regular expression is built from ∅, ε, alphabet symbols, union, concatenation, [[Kleene Star]], and grouping. It generates a [[Formal Language]] by interpreting those constructors as the corresponding operations on sets of strings.

A language is regular when some regular expression generates it. Practical search patterns add conveniences such as character classes, optional items, and one-or-more repetition, but features such as backreferences can exceed the power of formal regular expressions.

4600.title: Regression Robustness
4600.heading: Regression Robustness
4600.content:
Regression robustness is the stability of a substantive conclusion across reasonable model specifications, coding choices, and covariate sets. If the exposure estimate remains far from significance or retains a similar magnitude after defensible adjustments, the conclusion is less dependent on one arbitrary formula.

Robustness should be demonstrated with planned sensitivity analyses rather than declared from a single large model. A stable estimate can still be biased when all specifications share the same flawed measurement or selection process.

4603.title: Regular Element on a Module
4603.heading: Regular Element on a Module
4603.content:
An element r of a ring is regular on a module M when multiplication by r is injective on M. Equivalently, r is not a [[Zero Divisor on a Module]].

A [[Regular Sequence]] requires each element to be regular after quotienting by the preceding elements. Regularity therefore records independence successively rather than testing every element only on the original module.

4606.title: Regression Residual Plot
4606.heading: Regression Residual Plot
4606.content:
A regression residual plot graphs [[Residual|residuals]] against fitted values, predictors, or theoretical quantiles. A well-specified linear model should not leave an obvious trend or systematic change in residual spread.

Curvature can indicate violation of the [[Linearity Assumption]], while a funnel shape suggests nonconstant variance. Quantile–quantile residual plots assess distributional shape, and unusual isolated points may warrant investigation for data errors or influence.
